report.summary: Latency on demo-service jumped from a flat baseline within seconds, coinciding exactly with the database connection pool reaching its hard ceiling: all pool slots became used, waiters queued, and per-request connection wait rose sharply. Error logs appear a few seconds later reporting connection timeouts on /products and /orders returning HTTP 500, while request rate stayed flat and even dipped. Most probable cause: shared DB connection pool exhaustion, which queued requests, stalled the event loop and drove the p95 latency SLO breach.

timeline.event: Baseline: p95 latency 0.009468 s, pool_used 0, pool_pending 0, request rate 29.597 req/s.
Onset: pool_used jumps to 10 (at pool_max), pool_pending 36, p95 pool wait 0.883 s, event-loop delay p99 0.400 s, p95 latency 1.750 s.
First 'timeout exceeded when trying to connect' error log on /products (version 1.0.1).
Last of 5 connection-timeout 500s logged on /products and /orders.
Peak p95 latency 2.360 s with pool_pending 47 and p95 pool wait 1.870 s; http-latency-p95 rule fired.

hypotheses.statement: Exhaustion of the shared database connection pool caused the incident: all {pool_used_max} of {pool_max_max} connections were in use at 18:47:32 with {pending_max} requests waiting (obs_2, obs_3), p95 connection wait rose to {wait_max} s (obs_4) and event-loop delay p99 to {eld_max} s (obs_5), pushing p95 latency to {lat_max} s (obs_1) and then producing 'timeout exceeded when trying to connect' 500s (obs_7, obs_8); request rate did not rise (obs_6).

A CPU saturation / event-loop stall in demo-service caused the incident by delaying request handling, visible as event-loop delay p99 of {eld_max} s (obs_5) at the same time as the latency jump to {lat_max} s (obs_1); the stall begins simultaneously with the pool saturation and connection wait rather than before it (obs_2, obs_3, obs_4), so it is more consistent with a downstream effect of the pool.
A traffic surge caused the incident by overwhelming the service: request rate peaked at {req_max} req/s in the window (obs_6).

observations.statement: p95 latency was flat near {lat_base_min} s during the baseline window and stayed flat through 18:47:17, then jumped to {lat_first_jump} s at 18:47:32 and {lat_max} s at 18:47:47.
pool_used was 0 for the whole window until 18:47:32, when it reached {pool_used_max} connections, against a constant pool_max of {pool_max_max}.
pool_pending (requests waiting for a connection) went from 0 to {pending_first_jump} at 18:47:32 and then {pending_max} at 18:47:47, showing requests queueing for the pool.
p95 connection wait rose from ~{wait_base_min} s to {wait_first_jump} s at 18:47:32 and {wait_max} s at 18:47:47.
Event-loop delay p99 spiked from a baseline near {eld_base_first} s to {eld_max} s at 18:47:32 and {eld_last} s at 18:47:47, coincident with pool saturation.
Request rate stayed in a narrow band between {req_min} and {req_max} req/s and dipped at the onset, so no traffic surge accompanied the latency jump.

The only error log pattern in the window is 'request failed' with exception 'timeout exceeded when trying to connect', {p1_count} occurrences between 18:47:36.511Z and 18:47:44.630Z on service version 1.0.1.
Sample error log lines show HTTP status {log_status} with 'timeout exceeded when trying to connect' on routes /products and /orders, first at 18:47:36.511Z, version 1.0.1.

Log volume by severity shows error lines only at the end of the window ({err_sum} error lines), steady warn volume ({warn_min}-{warn_max} per minute) and roughly flat info volume ({info_min}-{info_max} per minute).

recommendations.action: Inspect for long-running or blocking database queries and leaked connection holders on the /products and /orders routes around 18:47:32 using DB session/connection-holder instrumentation.
recommendations.rationale: The pool was pinned at its ceiling with requests queued (hyp_1); a blocking query or missing connection release would explain all slots being held while request rate stayed flat.

recommendations.action: Review pool sizing (pool_max) against normal concurrency and consider raising it or adding a bounded wait-timeout with fast-fail to protect latency.
recommendations.rationale: Requests queued behind a pool_max of 10 connections until they timed out (hyp_1); more headroom or faster failure would limit latency propagation.

recommendations.action: Add alerting on pool_used/pool_max ratio, pool_pending and pool_wait_p95 so pool saturation is paged before the latency SLO is breached.
recommendations.rationale: Pool saturation preceded the error logs and the SLO breach (hyp_1), so it is a leading indicator.

recommendations.action: Capture CPU profile and event-loop blocking traces during the next occurrence to confirm whether the event-loop stall is purely pool-induced or has an independent CPU component.
recommendations.rationale: Event-loop delay p99 reached 0.400 s, which hyp_2 treats as a possible independent cause; profiling would separate the two.
